linked_companies.description: Focuses on the exploration, development, and production of crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids across a global portfolio of assets to supply worldwide energy markets.
linked_companies.evidence: ConocoPhillips operates as a pure-play Exploration and Production company, dedicating its entire business model to hydrocarbon extraction. Recent operational results demonstrate an enterprise production volume of over 2.3 million barrels of oil equivalent per day globally, with the U.S. Lower 48 basins contributing more than 1.45 million barrels daily. To sustain this output, the firm directs a $12 billion to $12.5 billion capital expenditure budget toward continuous drilling, completion efficiencies, and multi-well exploration programs, including the advancement of the Willow oil project in Alaska toward a 2029 start. Structurally, the company organizes its 9,700-person workforce and executive leadership into dedicated regional divisions focused exclusively on discovering, extracting, and processing crude oil, natural gas, and bitumen worldwide.
linked_companies.name: CONOCOPHILLIPS

linked_companies.description: Executes large-scale exploration, extraction, and processing of crude oil and natural gas across extensive global upstream assets to supply essential energy and petrochemical products.
linked_companies.evidence: ExxonMobil's fundamental corporate strategy and capital allocation are directly defined by the global extraction and refining of hydrocarbons. This core focus drives large-scale asset development, resulting in an 8% year-over-year global upstream production growth in Q2 2026, targeted yields of 1.8 million oil-equivalent barrels per day in the Permian, and ongoing offshore deepwater expansion across its Guyana block. The company supports these volumetric targets through a dedicated Upstream division and industry-first technological deployments, such as completing a fully autonomous deepwater well section and optimizing proprietary heavy oil extraction capabilities in Canada. These combined upstream operations recently culminated in the company's highest production outputs in over forty years, reaching 4.7 million oil-equivalent barrels per day backed by billions in targeted capital expenditures.
linked_companies.name: EXXONMOBIL HOLDINGS CORP

linked_companies.description: Produces and extracts crude oil and natural gas globally, operating extensive upstream assets dedicated to the exploration and development of hydrocarbon resources.
linked_companies.evidence: Chevron's foundational business model is anchored in its extensive hydrocarbon extraction capabilities, highlighted in recent reporting by U.S. production exceeding 2 million barrels of oil equivalent per day and key assets like the Permian Basin and TCO each surpassing 1 million barrels per day. To sustain this output and achieve a targeted 7% to 10% annual production growth, the company has allocated an $18 billion to $19 billion corporate capital budget specifically directed toward upstream asset optimization and global exploration. Furthermore, the strategic integration of legacy Hess assets, new deepwater project start-ups in the Gulf of Mexico, and expanding offshore operations across Guyana and the Eastern Mediterranean secure crude oil production as the primary structural driver of Chevron's commercial operations and cash flow.
linked_companies.name: CHEVRON CORP

linked_companies.description: Drives the exploration, development, and extraction of crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids across major global basins to supply international energy markets.
linked_companies.evidence: Occidental Petroleum operates as a near pure-play exploration and production company, driven by a core strategic focus on oil and gas development that yields over 1.42 million barrels of oil equivalent (BOE) per day. To sustain its 16.5 billion BOE resource base, the firm allocates between $5.5 billion and $5.9 billion in annual capital directly toward upstream extraction operations. This investment aggressively funds top-tier unconventional onshore developments, yielding new well performance 10% above industry averages, alongside extensive Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) programs. Furthermore, Occidental relies on specialized personnel like the Gulf of America team to manage its massive offshore extraction, characterized by 98% topside uptime, infrastructure-adjacent exploration successes such as the Bandit discovery, and advanced deepwater waterflood projects at Horn Mountain.
linked_companies.name: OCCIDENTAL PETROLEUM CORP

linked_companies.description: Processes crude oil and other feedstocks into transportation fuels and petrochemical products, playing a central role in the global hydrocarbon production and refining supply chain.

This strategic priority is structurally reinforced by a dedicated Refining segment and specialized executive leadership, including a Vice President of Crude & Feedstocks Supply & Trading, focused on efficiently sourcing heavy sour feedstocks. To bypass regional transit constraints and ensure physical delivery, the firm relies on its captive subsidiary, Antero Midstream, to construct and manage specialized pipeline gathering networks. This extraction and infrastructure framework fundamentally dictates the company's financial results, with natural gas sales generating $1.3 billion and accounting for over 67% of its total consolidated quarterly revenue.

Management actively optimizes this vast production scale via strategic supply curtailments during seasonal troughs and leverages its position as the nation's second-largest natural gas marketer to maintain an industry-leading cost structure.
